predecessors.name: Kingdom of Yugoslavia (Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes)
predecessors.text: the Kingdom of Yugoslavia's land as Cliopatria draws it in 1945 (250,300 km2); the monarchy gave way to the Federal People's Republic proclaimed on 29 November 1945

predecessors.name: Yugoslav Partisans
predecessors.text: Democratic Federal Yugoslavia, the Partisan-held land of 1944 (the page lists 'Democratic Federal Yugoslavia' as the infobox predecessor)

successors.name: Republic of Croatia
successors.text: Croatia, independence declared on 25 June 1991; part of its land was held by Serb forces to 1995

successors.name: North Macedonia
successors.text: Macedonia: referendum 8 September 1991, independence declared 25 September 1991

successors.name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
successors.text: Bosnia and Herzegovina: independence declared 3 March 1992

successors.name: Serbia and Montenegro (Federal Republic of Yugoslavia)
successors.text: the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia proclaimed by Serbia and Montenegro in April 1992, which 'claimed continuity to the former country'

successors.name: Croatian Republic of Herzeg-Bosnia
successors.text: the Croat-held land of Herzegovina and western Bosnia (the same reading as the croatian-republic-of-herzeg-bosnia dossier; the page lists no municipalities)

successors.name: Republika Srpska
successors.text: the Serb-held regions of Bosnia and Herzegovina (Natural Earth spells the region 'Repuplika Srpska')

ledger.x: 1945: the Federal People's Republic of Yugoslavia is proclaimed, 'on 29 November 1945'.
ledger.cpn: Kingdom of Yugoslavia (Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes)

ledger.x: 1945: the Julian March east of the Morgan Line is under Yugoslav military administration when the Federal People's Republic is proclaimed on 29 November 1945; the occupation is opened at the founding month because the state did not exist earlier, and it is inherited from the Yugoslav army's administration since…
1946: the Kingdom of Italy, owner of the occupied Julian March, ceases to exist.
1946: the Italian Republic becomes the owner of the same occupied land (republic-of-italy is founded from kingdom-of-italy in June 1946).
1947: the Julian March east of the Morgan Line stops being occupied land when the peace treaty takes effect on 15 September 1947; the cession itself is the next event.
1947: Italy cedes Istria, Fiume, Zara and most of Gorizia and Pola to Yugoslavia.
1947: Zone B of the Free Territory of Trieste is run by the Yugoslav army.
1954: the Free Territory ends as the London Memorandum, signed on 5 October 1954, shares it out; Zone B stays with Yugoslavia and Italian troops take over Zone A on 25 October.
1963: the Federal People's Republic becomes the Socialist Federal Republic.
1991: the Yugoslav army fights Slovenia after its declaration of 25 June.
1991: the Brioni Agreement of 7 July 1991 ends the fighting in Slovenia ('when the Brioni Accords were signed'; 'Slovenia and Croatia would postpone their independence for three months').
1991: the army and Serb forces hold a third of Croatia and press on Vukovar.
1991: the federation ceases to be a party to the Croatian front when it is declared dissolving.

wars.name: Ten-Day War
wars.outcome: Slovenia left the federation; the Brioni Agreement of 7 July 1991 imposed a three-month moratorium during which the army's withdrawal, begun about ten days later, was completed by 26 October 1991.

wars.name: Croatian War of Independence
wars.outcome: The war as a whole runs from 1 March 1991 to 12 November 1995 (infobox), but the SFRY's part ends with its dissolution in 1991 (the span here is held to the state's life).

certainty.note: The Julian March (Morgan Line) and Trieste were provisional and in dispute; the other frontiers are those of the Kingdom.

The Italian frontier is the 1947 peace treaty's; Zone B of the Free Territory is provisional to the 1954 London Memorandum, formalised by the Treaty of Osimo (ratified 1977); the other frontiers were not examined on the pages opened.
The front lines in Croatia (the Serb-held third) and the republics' claims were moving; the Slovenian line is the republic border.
